The problem isn't always too much stuff

It's the tangle.
The pile. The gap.
The things that never fit.

Cables collect behind the desk. Small things slide around in drawers. Pipes interrupt the space under the sink. A stool or shelf takes up just a little too much room beside the toilet.

Standard organizers come in standard sizes. Your home has its own dimensions, obstacles, and routines—so you end up working around the product instead of making the space work for you.

↳

When everything has a place that fits, staying organized gets simpler. Less looking for things. Less moving one thing to reach another. Less visual clutter.

One idea: make the fit work for you.

A place for every cable.

Cable organizers for desks, devices, and everyday connections.

Loose cords tangle, trail across surfaces, and disappear behind furniture. Plan an organized route around your devices and the space available, so cables stay grouped and easier to find.

↳ A cleaner-looking setup, with the connections you use in reach.

Work around the pipes.

Custom-fit shelving and organization for under-sink spaces.

Bottles pile up below while the space above goes unused. Shelving shaped around the cabinet and plumbing gives towels, cleaning supplies, and everyday essentials their own place.

↳ Use the awkward gaps and empty height you already have.

Open it. Find it. Put it back.

Drawer inserts, dividers, and organization inside cabinets.

A jumble of small things is hard to keep tidy. Plan compartments and storage around the interior dimensions and the items you keep there, so each thing has a place to return to.

↳ Less rummaging through drawers and rearranging cabinet shelves.

Make room around the toilet.

Custom toilet stools, plus organization for the surrounding space.

A standard stool can crowd the floor, while narrow gaps around the toilet go unused. Plan a stool around the fixture and available space, or explore storage for toilet paper and other bathroom essentials.

↳ A more considered fit in one of the home's tightest spaces.

Before you plan your space

A few practical
questions.

What does SpaceMax offer?+

Our range covers cable organization, under-sink shelving and storage, organization inside drawers and cabinets, custom toilet stools, and storage around the toilet. Each starts with the space available and what you need to do with it.

What does “custom fit” mean?+

It means planning around the actual dimensions, obstacles, and items in your space. The relevant details change by product: a cable route, a drainpipe, a drawer opening, or the shape and clearance around a toilet. Measurements need to be reviewed before any final design.

Are toilet stools and toilet-area storage different products?+

Yes. A custom toilet stool is a separate product planned around the toilet and available floor space. Toilet-area organization makes use of the surrounding space for bathroom essentials. You can select either one in the planner.

What should I measure?+

Choose a solution in the planner for specific prompts. In general, record the usable width, depth, and height, then note anything that affects fit or access. Photos and the dimensions of the items you want to organize are helpful for a later design discussion.

Can I buy here yet?+

This site is a product preview. Final product details, pricing, and ordering are not configured yet. The planner keeps your space details in your browser and lets you download them; it does not send a request, place an order, or take a payment.
